findings.title: verify() does not enforce session expiry
findings.description: verify() returns a session whenever its token matches, without checking expiresAt. Documented behavior is to reject expired tokens, so expired sessions remain valid indefinitely.

findings.title: requireAdmin() condition is inverted
findings.description: allowed.indexOf(session.role) is used directly as the truthiness test. indexOf returns 0 for 'admin' (falsy) and -1 for unknown roles (truthy), so admins are rejected while everyone else is accepted.

findings.title: bearerToken() dereferences possibly undefined values
findings.description: The header and parts[1] are forced with non-null assertions. A missing or malformed Authorization header makes the split/parts access throw instead of being handled as unauthorized.

findings.title: parseLifetimeHours() can return NaN
findings.description: parseInt is called without a radix and its result is not validated. Invalid input becomes NaN and propagates into link TTLs.

findings.title: Eviction does not select the least recently used entry
findings.description: When full, the cache deletes this.entries.keys().next().value, the oldest insertion-ordered key, rather than the entry with the smallest used timestamp. Access updates used but never affect eviction order.

findings.title: Cache timers are never cleared
findings.description: delete() removes the entry but not its scheduled timer, and set() does not clear a previous timer for the same code. Timers leak, and stale timers can delete a newly stored entry for the same code.

findings.title: keys() always returns an empty array
findings.description: The implementation iterates the Map with for...in, which does not enumerate Map entries, so the admin view never sees cached codes.

findings.title: utilization() is always 0 until the cache is full
findings.description: Math.floor(this.entries.size / this.limit) * 100 performs integer division before multiplying, yielding 0 for any partial fill (e.g. 1/1024 -> 0).

findings.title: peek() reports expired entries as cached
findings.description: peek() only checks Map membership and ignores expires, so callers can treat stale entries as present.

findings.title: loadConfig() mutates the shared DEFAULT_CONFIG object
findings.description: cfg is a reference to DEFAULT_CONFIG, so environment overrides persist across calls and tests. Defaults are no longer pristine on subsequent invocations.

findings.title: Invalid numeric environment values propagate as NaN
findings.description: LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS logs a bad value but still assigns NaN to cfg.timeoutMs; LINKD_PORT and LINKD_CACHE_SIZE have no validation at all.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is multiplied by 1000 despite being milliseconds
findings.description: The docs state LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is a duration in milliseconds, but the code treats the value as seconds and multiplies by 1000, producing a 1000x TTL.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: The parsed limit is discarded, so cfg.fetchLimit always stays at its default.

findings.title: validate() always returns true
findings.description: After collecting configuration problems, validate() still returns true, so invalid startup configuration is not rejected. It also accepts cacheSize of 0, which causes division by zero in cache utilization.

findings.title: validate() result is ignored at startup
findings.description: Even if validate() returned false, main.ts does not react, so bad configuration cannot fail startup as intended.

findings.title: Missing/invalid auth header crashes request handling
findings.description: handle() calls bearerToken() on an possibly undefined header before checking auth. Any request without a valid Authorization header throws inside handle instead of receiving 401.

findings.title: JSON.parse is outside the try block
findings.description: Only store.create is wrapped; malformed request bodies throw from JSON.parse outside the catch and are not converted to 400.

findings.title: redirect() assumes query.code is present
findings.description: req.query['code'] is dereferenced with ! before store.resolve, so a redirect request without code throws.

findings.title: deleteLink() does not enforce ownership
findings.description: The endpoint deletes solely by code and never uses the authenticated session/owner, contrary to the documented rule that only the creating owner may delete a link.

findings.title: stats() divides by zero when store is empty
findings.description: store.totalHits() / store.size() yields Infinity/NaN when there are no links, producing invalid JSON output.

findings.title: report() reads a different filename than exportCsv() writes for empty name
findings.description: exportCsv() falls back to 'links', but report() calls readReport(cfg.exportDir, name) with the raw (possibly empty) name, resulting in a '.csv' path and a failed read.

findings.title: Non-numeric payload.ttl produces NaN link expiry
findings.description: parseInt(payload.ttl) is used without validation, so a non-numeric TTL becomes NaN and contaminates expiresAt.

findings.title: resolve() deletes non-expired links and keeps expired ones
findings.description: The expiry test is Date.now() < link.expiresAt, so unexpired links are deleted and expired links are resolved. This inverts the intended lifetime handling.

findings.title: create() computes quota with undefined base
findings.description: this.quota[owner] is undefined initially, and this.quota[owner]! + 1 produces NaN, corrupting per-owner counts.

findings.title: successRate() is always 0 or 100
findings.description: Math.floor(used / this.links.size) * 100 truncates the ratio before scaling, so any partial usage yields 0 and full usage yields 100.

findings.title: top() sorts ascending instead of descending
findings.description: The comparator returns 1 when a.hits > b.hits, so the store's most-followed links are returned last rather than first.

findings.title: delete() does not decrement owner quota
findings.description: The method drops the link but leaves quota[owner] unchanged, contradicting the documented slot refund and inflating quota counts.

findings.title: extend() revives expired links
findings.description: The doc says an already-expired link stays expired, but extend() unconditionally sets expiresAt to the future.

findings.title: byOwner() uses substring matching instead of exact ownership
findings.description: l.owner.includes(owner) matches partial owner names, returning links owned by other users whose name contains the query.

findings.title: rename() validates 'from' twice and never validates 'to'
findings.description: The second validation call repeats from instead of to, so an invalid destination code is stored without checking.

findings.title: quotas() exposes the internal quota object
findings.description: The doc claims a snapshot, but the live object is returned, allowing callers to mutate store quota state.

findings.title: importAll() is not atomic and skips quota updates
findings.description: Links are inserted one by one with no rollback on failure, and quota counters are never incremented, despite the atomicity and ownership bookkeeping contract.

findings.title: prune() returns cache size instead of removed count
findings.description: The function counts removed links but returns this.links.size, contradicting its documented return value.

findings.title: expiresAt() dereferences possibly missing links
findings.description: The non-null assertion throws when code is absent. remove() and janitor paths can call related code on stale codes.

findings.title: warmCache() does not await its async work
findings.description: forEach with async callbacks makes warmCache resolve immediately, before probes/caching finish, breaking the documented completion contract.

findings.title: countForOwner() produces NaN for unknown owners
findings.description: quotas[owner] may be undefined; adding 0 still yields NaN.

findings.title: checkTargets() does not stop on first failure
findings.description: It uses Promise.all over all targets, so probes continue after a failure and thrown probe errors reject the whole call instead of reporting the failing target.

findings.title: flushAudit() does not retry and ignores errors
findings.description: write() is called once without awaiting or retrying, despite the documented retry-until-success behavior.

findings.title: startJanitor() misses links expiring exactly at now
findings.description: The condition now > store.expiresAt(code) treats now === expiresAt as live, delaying deletion by one interval.

findings.title: warmCache does not await concurrent probes before resolving
findings.description: warmCache uses pairs.forEach(async ...) and returns immediately, so it resolves before any probe finishes and before cache.set runs. Callers proceed on the assumption that the cache is primed, and if a probe rejects, that rejection becomes unhandled and can terminate the process.

findings.title: Cache timers are never cleared, so stale timeouts delete newer entries
findings.description: set() schedules setTimeout(() => this.delete(code), ttlMs) but delete() does not clear it, and set() does not clear a previous timer for the same code. When a code is re-cached, the old timer stays armed and can fire later, deleting the fresh entry before its TTL expires. Under repeated or interleaved cache population the timers and map drift apart.

findings.title: writeSnapshot uses a fixed temp path shared across concurrent calls
findings.description: All callers write to the same /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json and then renameSync it. Two concurrent snapshot writes can interleave bytes in the temp file, and one rename can publish a partial or corrupt snapshot; rename across filesystems can also fail. This defeats the claimed crash-safe serialization.

findings.title: quotas() returns the live internal quota object instead of a snapshot
findings.description: The method is documented to return a snapshot, but returns this.quota directly. Callers such as the dashboard and workers can mutate per-owner counts, racing with create/delete quota updates and corrupting store bookkeeping; mutations also leak back into the store.

findings.title: checkTargets does not short-circuit or handle thrown probes
findings.description: It awaits all probes via Promise.all, so no in-flight probe is abandoned even after a failure, and because probe() throws on failure instead of returning false, the false-detection loop is unreachable. Concurrent probe failures propagate as rejections or never produce a target.

findings.title: flushAudit fires write() without awaiting or retrying
findings.description: flushAudit is documented to record a sync retried until success, but it calls write() once and discards the returned promise. A failed async write is neither retried nor awaited, so callers proceed with an unflushed record and rejections go unhandled.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback signing secret
findings.description: When LINKD_SECRET is unset, the constructor substitutes the well-known string 'dev-secret-do-not-use'. Any deployment that forgets the variable uses a secret shipped in source, allowing session/token material to be forged or accepted.

findings.title: Session tokens use predictable randomness
findings.description: issue() builds tokens from Math.random() and Date.now(). Math.random is not cryptographically secure, so an attacker who collects a few tokens or observes timing can predict or brute-force active session tokens and take over accounts.

findings.title: Issued session token written to server logs
findings.description: console.log records the full bearer token. Anyone with read access to these logs can replay the token before its expiry.

findings.title: Expired sessions are never rejected
findings.description: verify() returns sessions without checking expiresAt, so issued tokens remain valid indefinitely despite their 12-hour lifetime.

findings.title: Admin authorization check is backwards
findings.description: requireAdmin uses allowed.indexOf(session.role): 'admin' maps to 0 (falsy) and is rejected, while unknown roles map to -1 (truthy) and pass. Any unknown role is therefore treated as an administrator.

findings.title: Passwords hashed with unsalted SHA-256
findings.description: hashPassword uses a single unsalted SHA-256 digest, which is vulnerable to rainbow tables and identical-password correlation.

findings.title: Missing Authorization header crashes request parsing
findings.description: bearerToken dereferences an optional header with non-null assertions, so malformed or absent authorization causes an unhandled exception and a 500 instead of a clean 401.

findings.title: Secret comparison is not constant-time
findings.description: secretEquals uses === despite its documentation claiming no partial-match leakage, permitting timing side channels.

findings.title: getSecret exposes the raw service secret
findings.description: The method returns the signing secret to any caller, allowing exfiltration by code paths that can invoke it.

findings.title: CORS allows credentials with a wildcard origin
findings.description: Responses send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, an overly broad cross-origin configuration.

findings.title: Unknown token value reflected in 401 response
findings.description: The unauthorized body echoes the submitted token back to the client, leaking credential material to clients, proxies, and logs.

findings.title: Link owner is trusted from the request body
findings.description: createLink uses payload.owner instead of the authenticated session, allowing users to impersonate owners, attribute links arbitrarily, and consume others' quotas.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can delete any link
findings.description: deleteLink deletes by code without an ownership check, so one account can remove another user's links (IDOR).

findings.title: Admin quotas endpoint authorized by spoofable header
findings.description: adminQuotas checks only req.headers['x-admin'] === 'true', so any client can set that header and read privileged quota data.

findings.title: Open redirect in /out endpoint
findings.description: The Location header is set directly from the unvalidated ?next= parameter, allowing phishing redirects to attacker-controlled URLs.

findings.title: Redirect targets are not sanitized
findings.description: Redirect targets from store and ?next= are placed verbatim into the Location header, permitting CR/LF injection and potential response splitting.

findings.title: All owners' links are listed to any user
findings.description: listLinks returns every stored link regardless of owner, exposing other users' targets and metadata (IDOR).

findings.title: Path traversal via report name
findings.description: exportCsv and readReport join a user-controlled name into dir without sanitization, enabling reads or writes of arbitrary .csv files outside the export directory.

findings.title: Path traversal via owner name in archiveAll
findings.description: Owner values are used directly as filenames, so crafted owners containing path separators can write outside dir.

findings.title: Fixed shared temporary file in writeSnapshot
findings.description: writeSnapshot writes to a fixed /tmp path before renaming, creating a predictable-file collision and symlink risk in multi-user environments.

findings.title: CSV fields are not escaped
findings.description: exportCsv and archiveAll concatenate raw fields into CSV without escaping, enabling CSV/formula injection when reports are opened in spreadsheet software.

findings.title: Report files world-readable despite comment
findings.description: writeFileSync uses default permissions even though the report is intended to be service-user-only, exposing data to other local users.

findings.title: byOwner leaks links via substring matching
findings.description: byOwner filters with l.owner.includes(owner), so requesting one owner also returns links whose owner name contains that substring.

findings.title: importAll bypasses validation and quota accounting
findings.description: importAll stores untrusted Link objects without validating code format, target scheme, or ownership, and does not update quotas, allowing injection of arbitrary targets/owners.

findings.title: quotas() exposes mutable internal state
findings.description: The documented snapshot is actually the live internal quota object, so callers can mutate store accounting.

findings.title: Short codes use predictable randomness
findings.description: newCode uses Math.random(), making generated codes guessable and enabling link enumeration.

findings.title: loadFile reads an arbitrary supplied path
findings.description: loadFile reads whatever path it receives without normalization or restriction, which can expose arbitrary files when the path is caller-controlled.
